comparison: Strong agreement on the core contribution of thrifty CNNs. Both recognize the model architecture (C56-C65), parameter efficiency (C5, C64, C115, C65), and performance improvements (C6, C77, C117). OpenEval provides technical detail about linear parameter scaling (C63), while peer reviewers emphasize the 'clever' solution and complete data separation. Both evaluations are highly positive.

Perfect alignment on methodological approach (C37-C45). Both affirm the research objective, data processing strategy, and use of out-of-frame sequences. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the 'well motivated and defined problem' and 'complete separation of training and test data,' while OpenEval notes the 'sound rationale' and 'essential methodological context.'

Complete agreement on the key finding that two training approaches yield different results (C9-C10, C111-C113, C132-C136). Both treat this as a significant discovery. OpenEval notes the speculative nature of explanations (C134-C137), while peer reviewers call it 'surprising' and highlight its implications for understanding germinal center function.

Full agreement on the value of open-source contributions (C35-C36). Both explicitly praise the software release and reproducibility tools. Peer reviewers emphasize 'practical value for the community,' while OpenEval notes 'good scientific practice for reproducibility and community benefit.'

Strong agreement on data limitations (C109-C110, C141-C142). Both acknowledge scarcity of high-quality out-of-frame sequence data as a constraint. OpenEval provides detailed technical explanation (C172-C175) about database coverage, while peer reviewers and editor emphasize this limitation affects all current machine-learning methods.

Agreement that elaborations like per-site rates and transformers did not improve performance (C107-C108, C120, C127, C86-C88). OpenEval provides detailed methodological critique of previous work (C121-C126) and theoretical explanation (C129), while peer reviewers accept the finding and attribute it to data availability constraints.

Agreement on the surprising finding that tang data outperformed held-out briney data (C81), with both accepting the sequencing error explanation (C82-C85). Peer reviewers do not challenge this observation, treating it as part of careful data curation that they praise.

Agreement on the conclusion that biological effects may exist but don't substantially improve statistical models (C8, C128-C130). Both accept this finding without challenge. OpenEval provides measured interpretation citing mechanistic modeling work, while peer reviewers present it as a key result without critique.

Agreement on DeepSHM comparison showing thrifty CNNs match performance with fewer parameters (C89-C97). Peer reviewers explicitly state thrifty CNNs 'match the performance of significantly larger models like DeepSHM,' while OpenEval details parameter counts and computational efficiency, both supporting the efficiency thesis.

Agreement on validation methodology (C78-C80). Peer reviewers explicitly commend efforts to communicate with previous model developers and use strongest versions for comparison. OpenEval describes this as part of performance comparison methodology. Both treat this as a methodological strength.

Partial overlap on modest improvements being interesting given biological motivation (C117-C119, C130-C131). OpenEval provides nuanced interpretation about limitations of statistical approaches, while peer reviewers focus on the efficiency achievement. Both acknowledge the biological context but emphasize different aspects.

OpenEval evaluates model fit methodology and finding that model differences are smaller than dataset differences (C98-C106, supported by Figure 3). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific methodological claims about model fit assessment.

OpenEval evaluates dataset descriptions and detailed data processing methods including phylogenetic inference, filtering criteria, and sequence alignment (C51-C55, C144-C162). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these detailed methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates metric definitions and appropriateness (C70-C76), including AUROC interpretation, AUPRC rationale for imbalanced data, R-precision, and substitution accuracy. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific metric choices.

OpenEval evaluates jaffe dataset processing methodology for synonymous mutations (C163-C167), including identification and masking of fourfold degenerate sites. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific data processing claims.

OpenEval evaluates training procedure details including loss functions, weighting scheme, and training duration (C168-C171). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these training implementation details.

OpenEval evaluates background and motivation sections covering established immunological knowledge, existing SHM models, and biological motivation for wider context models (C1-C2, C11-C32). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these introductory and background claims.
